meta.title: Operation of Slide Projector in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To project microscopic images of plant tissue slides, permanent slide sets, and photomicrographs for teaching, demonstration, and identification of crude drugs in Pharmacognosy practicals.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for projecting prepared glass slides and photographic transparencies during demonstration sessions and practical examinations.
procedure: Place the slide projector on a stable table at an appropriate distance from the projection screen (typically 2–4 meters for a standard classroom screen).
Connect the projector to the power supply and switch ON the cooling fan first if a separate switch exists.
Allow the lamp to warm up for 2–3 minutes before inserting slides.
Darken the room by closing curtains or switching off lights for maximum image clarity.
Insert the glass slide or photographic transparency into the slide carrier with the emulsion/image side facing the correct direction (test with a blank slide first).
Place the slide carrier into the projector gate.
Adjust the focus using the focus ring until the projected image is sharp and clear.
Adjust the zoom if available to fit the image to the screen.
For sequential demonstration, advance through slides using the remote control or manual advance button.
After the session, switch OFF the projection lamp first and allow the cooling fan to run for 3–5 minutes before switching off completely.
Remove slides and store them carefully in their labelled slide boxes.
Cover the projector with its dust cover when not in use.
Log usage (date, operator, slides used) in the equipment log.
precautions: Never switch off the projector abruptly during operation — always switch the lamp off first and allow the fan to cool the lamp.
Do not look directly into the projection lens while the lamp is on — the light is intense and can cause eye injury.
Handle glass slides with care — cracked slides can shatter when heated by the projection lamp.
Ensure adequate ventilation around the projector — the lamp generates significant heat.
Replace projector lamps only when cool and using gloves — skin oils on bulb surface cause premature failure.
Store glass slides horizontally in their designated boxes to prevent slippage and breakage.
Do not place fingers on the optical elements (lens, condenser) — use only approved lens cleaning tissues.
